steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Selection criteria: function, aesthetics, cost (material + processing + assembly), availability, sustainability (recyclability, material miles), manufacturability.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Decision matrix: weighted scoring system - list criteria, assign weights, score each option, multiply weight x score, total reveals best choice. Removes bias.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Working properties must match function: frying pan handle needs thermal insulation (thermoset/silicone), not conductivity (metal). Bicycle frame needs strength-to-weight (aluminium/CFRP).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Batch vs mass production affects material choice: mass production justifies injection moulding tooling; batch uses CNC or hand-laid composites.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Justify with SPECIFIC criteria - 'tensile strength of 500 MPa exceeds the requirement of 200 MPa' Use a decision matrix when asked to compare or evaluate Consider at least 4 criteria: function, cost, sustainability and one other
